title: Local AI on your computer: private, offline, free · {name}
description: Run AI locally without internet: download it once (3.1 GB), then it answers in your browser. No account, nothing to install. Needs 12 GB of memory.
h1: AI on your own computer, even offline.
lede: Download it once ({size}) and it answers right here in your browser, with no internet, no account and nothing to install. It needs a computer with {memory} of memory and a recent graphics chip, not a phone, and its answers are simpler and slower than a big online AI’s.
cta: Get the AI on this computer
pane.ask: Help me write to my landlord about the damp in the bedroom. Firm, but polite.
pane.answer: Here’s a draft: “Dear Mr Martin, since early October the bedroom wall has been damp and the paint is peeling. Could you send someone to look at it this month?”
pane.title: A letter written in {name}, offline
needs.title: Will it run on your computer?
needs.why: {name} checks first. On a computer that can’t run it, it isn’t offered at all, and this page’s button opens the other AIs instead.
needs.rows: A recent graphics chip your browser can use (WebGPU)
Chrome or Edge. Safari and Firefox where their graphics support allows it
A computer. Not a phone or a tablet
needs.else: {name} still works, with an AI online instead: a free account at a provider, a plan you already pay for, or your organisation’s own. What {name} keeps stays on your computer either way.
needs.local: Already run Ollama or LM Studio? {name} can answer through it too, once that app allows this site.
needs.crash: If loading the AI ever closes the tab, {name} stops offering it in that browser.
how.title: Downloaded once. Then no internet needed.
how.why: No program to install: your browser keeps it, as it keeps a page.
how.steps: Open the AI on this computer in {name}’s settings. {name} checks this computer first.
Download it once: {size}. You can keep using {name} while it comes.
Turn off Wi-Fi: it keeps answering, and the box says so.
how.speed: Each time you open {name}, it loads from your computer before its first answer. Then, on a fast computer, its first words come in under a second. A smaller computer is slower.
how.source: Measured on {date} on an M3 Max, once loaded: first words after {chromium} in Chrome’s engine, {webkit} in Safari’s.
private.title: Private, and you can check.
private.why: There’s no {name} server. With the AI on your computer, what you write stays on it, unless you have {name} search the web or send something.
private.cards: Your request and its answer are written in this browser tab. The shield under each answer says so, from your browser’s own record of what the page sent.
Your conversations and files are encrypted on your computer. Clearing the browser’s data deletes them, unless you made a backup.
What it writes carries a hidden mark, as the EU’s AI Act asks of AI text. Its answers are no worse for it, and anyone can check a long one.
private.check: Check a text for the mark
also.title: What else works offline.
also.why: Once you’ve opened {name} with a connection, it opens again without one.
also.yesItems: Your conversations, your files and everything {name} keeps.
Dictation, done on your computer, after a small download the first time.
Answers read aloud, by a voice on your computer.
also.noItems: Searching the web, unless you set up an offline library: Wikipedia from a Kiwix server.
Working numbers out with code, and pages in answers: in Chrome and Edge, they need a connection to start.
Your connected services, such as email or a drive.
versus.title: What it does less well than a big online AI.
versus.why: It’s a small AI, made to fit on a computer. Here is the difference, plainly.
versus.rows: A long report, not a book
Only what it learned, unless it can search
To its provider, on its terms
Free with limits, or paid, with an account
versus.both: You don’t have to choose. Add an online AI too: with {auto}, {name} answers with the one on your computer while you’re offline, and “{keep}” keeps everything there, for a whole project if you like.
work.title: At work, your organisation’s own AI.
work.why: A company or a public body can have {name} answer only through its own AI service, on servers it chooses, with its sign-in and its rules.
limits.title: What it doesn’t do.
limits.items: Run on a phone or a tablet.
Run on a computer with less than {memory} of memory, or no recent graphics chip.
See pictures, or look up recent facts while you’re offline.
Answer as well as a big online AI: check what matters.
Work numbers out with code offline, in Chrome and Edge.
Survive clearing the browser’s data: the download goes, and so does what {name} keeps, unless you made a backup.
faq.title: Your questions.
faq.items: Yes. The AI is a free download, {name} is free and open source, and there’s no account to make, at {name} or anywhere else.
Does it work on my phone?
Not the AI on the computer: it needs more than a phone or a tablet can give it. On a phone, {name} works with an online AI.
Gemma 4 E2B, an AI Google publishes openly, converted for browsers and downloaded from Hugging Face at a version {name} fixes. It reads and writes more than 140 languages.
How do I know nothing leaves?
Turn off Wi-Fi and ask something. And under each answer, a shield shows it was written on this computer, from your browser’s own record.
Does it slow my computer down?
While it answers, it works the graphics chip hard, and {name} keeps the page still meanwhile. Loaded, it takes about {loaded} of memory, which is why it needs {memory}.
Not the web. It can search an offline library: Wikipedia and other books from a Kiwix server, on your computer, at school or at work.
end.why: Opens the AI on this computer in {name}’s settings, and nothing downloads until you choose. On a computer that can’t run it, the settings open on the other AIs instead.
